ov: About 197 species of megabats, including the flying foxes, the family with the largest bats. Most are nocturnal or active at dusk, eat fruit or nectar, and find food by sight and smell rather than echolocation. Some roost in colonies of up to a million.
wt: Up to 1.45 kg; a third of species weigh under 50 g
rg: Tropical and subtropical Africa, Asia and Oceania; Papua New Guinea has the most species.
df: Mostly fruit and nectar, plus leaves, pollen, seed pods and sap.
fx: Some captive megabats have lived more than 30 years.
A quarter of species are threatened, mainly by habitat loss and hunting for food.
